rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial noun for someone who tells stories to an audience.

example.english: This storyteller tells stories at the cha chaan teng all the time, and all the neighbours love listening.
example.traditional: 呢個講故佬成日喺茶記講古，街坊個個都鍾意聽。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gong2 gu2 lou2 seng4 jat6 hai2 caa4 gei3 gong2 gu2 gaai1 fong1 go3 go3 dou1 zung1 ji3 teng1

rows.note: Use this for a professional or traditional public storyteller, especially one performing narrated stories.

example.english: In the teahouse, once the storyteller began, the whole audience fell silent.
example.traditional: 茶館入面，說書人一開腔，成班客就靜晒。
example.jyutping: caa4 gun2 jap6 min6 syut3 syu1 jan4 jat1 hoi1 hong1 seng4 baan1 haak3 zau6 zing6 saai3

rows.note: Use this when “storyteller” means a person who habitually tells lies or fibs.

example.english: That storyteller is a liar; they can even make up a story about being late.
example.traditional: 佢係個大話精，連自己遲到都可以作故仔。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 go3 daai6 waa6 zing1 lin4 zi6 gei2 ci4 dou3 dou1 ho2 ji5 zok3 gu3 zai2
